fullPassage: In the busy city of Boston, two friends, Amy and Riley, found themselves at the starting line of the famous Boston Marathon. Their excitement bubbled over. Eager to ensure they were fully prepared for the challenge ahead, they arrived two hours before the scheduled start time. As the race began, Riley said, "I'm feeling a mix of excitement and nerves right now, but knowing you're by my side makes it all better." "Don't worry," Amy reassured her friend with a confident smile. "We've dedicated ourselves to training for this race for over a year now." As they approached the halfway mark, however, disaster struck. Riley slipped on an uneven piece of road, her ankle twisting painfully. Amy rushed to her friend's side, her heart heavy with worry. Riley said, with her voice showing signs of discomfort from the pain, "I don't know if I can keep going. My ankle... It's too much." "We've come too far to give up now, Riley. We'll get through this together. Lean on me if you need to," said Amy. Despite Riley's protests, Amy insisted on supporting her friend through the difficult moments ahead. With Riley's arm resting over Amy's shoulder, they adjusted their pace, sharing the burden as they pressed on, one step at a time. The miles stretched endlessly before them, but the cheers of the crowd echoed, carrying Amy and Riley onward. A lot of them shouted together, "You can do it!" Finally, they reached the last corner. The finish line appeared in the distance, like a light of hope. Tears of joy flowed freely as Amy and Riley crossed the finish line hand in hand. "Amy, you were my rock. Whenever I felt like giving up, you were there to push me forward." In that moment, they knew that they had achieved something far greater than just completing a marathon — they had conquered their fears, overcome obstacles, and proven that with the support of a true friend by your side, anything is possible.

questions.passage:
(A) The children threw a small <u>rock</u> into the river and watched it sink to the bottom.

(B) Riley told Amy, "You were my <u>rock</u>; whenever I felt like giving up, you pushed me forward."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 rock의 문맥적 의미가 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: rock: (A) 돌 (명사) (B) 든든한 버팀목이 되어 주는 사람 (명사·비유)
det.analysis:
✅ ① (A) 돌 - (B) 든든한 버팀목: (A)는 강에 던진 '돌', (B)는 Riley가 Amy를 '든든한 버팀목'이라 부른 것 ← 정답
❌ ② (A) 든든한 버팀목 - (B) 돌: 둘 다 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (A) 돌 - (B) 돌: (B)는 사람(버팀목)이므로 오류
❌ ④ (A) 든든한 버팀목 - (B) 든든한 버팀목: (A)는 실제 돌이므로 오류
det.tip: rock: 돌(물체) vs 든든한 버팀목(비유적 사람). You were my rock=너는 나의 버팀목이었어

det.analysis:
✅ ① obstacle(장애물): 길을 막고 목표를 어렵게 하는 것=장애물의 정의 ← 정답
❌ ② shortcut(지름길): 더 쉽게 가는 길
❌ ③ reward(보상): 노력의 대가
❌ ④ signal(신호): 정보를 전하는 표시
det.tip: obstacle=장애물. overcome obstacles=장애물을 극복하다

questions.passage: As they approached the halfway mark, however, disaster struck. Riley slipped on an uneven piece of road, her ankle __________ (twist) painfully. Amy rushed to her friend's side, her heart heavy with worry.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: twist → twisting: 'her ankle'를 의미상 주어로 하는 분사구문(독립분사구문, 현재분사)
det.analysis: twist(동사원형) → twisting(현재분사). 'her ankle __________ painfully'는 앞 절과 콤마로 이어지는 분사구문으로, 의미상 주어 her ankle이 '비틀리는' 상황을 동시에 묘사. 능동·진행의 의미라 현재분사 twisting.
det.tip: 분사구문(부대상황): 명사 + V-ing. her ankle twisting painfully=발목이 고통스럽게 비틀리면서

questions.passage: As the race began, Riley said that she was feeling a mix of excitement and nerves, but that knowing you are by my side __________ (make) it all better.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: make → makes: 주어가 동명사구 knowing ...이므로 단수 취급, 동사는 makes
det.analysis: make(동사원형) → makes(3인칭 단수 동사). 주어가 동명사구 'knowing you are by my side(네가 곁에 있다는 것을 아는 것)'로, 동명사 주어는 단수 취급하므로 동사는 단수형 makes가 와야 한다.
det.tip: 동명사 주어 = 단수 취급. Knowing ... makes it better(O). 'knowing'이 이끄는 긴 주어의 핵심은 단수
